story: On a breezy, clear Monday night in Sumter Oaks, Gary is marching determinedly down Magnolia Loop toward Town Square while the rest of the neighborhood settles in. At Rosa's House, Donna is cheerfully recruiting Hal for a Tuesday pickleball match she and Gary are planning, and Hal responds with his usual dry wit, asking for the gravy and wondering aloud how many flamingos are on the lawn. Rosa, content as ever, reminds Hal that his Thursday morning coffee date on her porch is set in ink and urges him to sit down and eat before the pot roast disappears.

gary.thought_process: I've got the Architectural Review form in hand, and it's past 9 PM on a Monday. Filing it is the right thing to do for the parade lights, and the form is for Town Hall, so I should head to the town square, where the Town Hall is, and get it in order. Nobody's around on the street to talk to. Donna and Hal were right that I should do this by the book, and I'd rather have the paperwork done than risk trouble over an unapproved cart. Quiet hours start at 10, so I'll keep the sound system plans on paper for now. Moving to town_square is the next step toward the goal.

parameters.content: Heading to the town square to get my cart modification form filed with Architectural Review so the parade lights are legit.

donna.thought_process: Supper's winding down, Hal just arrived, and Rosa wrote their coffee in ink. I've already taken my seat, so no need to keep fussing with the table. My real goal is the pickleball ladder, and Gary's Tuesday session is booked, but I've got Hal in front of me and he's a regular at things. A little social stirring is my specialty: tease Hal about his flamingo counts and see if he'd come cheer from the sidelines or even scout for a fourth. Keep it short and warm, and don't repeat anything already said at the table.

parameters.content: Hal, you're just in time, and don't think I missed that you got roped into coffee with Rosa. Tuesday morning Gary and I are hitting the pickleball courts if you want to come keep score and heckle us.

hal.thought_process: Supper's on at Rosa's and Donna's sitting right there, the very woman whose flamingo count I'm supposed to be verifying. Rosa wrote coffee in ink, so I'm obligated to be civil. I can't count flamingos from a dining table, but I can take the measure of the suspect over dinner. A gruff, dry remark keeps things friendly and lets me fish for her count without starting a fight on a full stomach.

parameters.content: Evening, Donna. Pass the gravy, and while you're at it, tell me honestly how many flamingos are on that lawn tonight. I'd hate to count them myself in the morning.

rosa.thought_process: Everyone's at my table now, Donna's eating, Hal just teased me about the coffee in ink. I've already written it in the schedule, so I don't need to ask again. Best thing now is to answer Hal warmly and nail down a real time, since this goal has slipped before. It's 9:17 PM, so I should be mindful of the evening too, but a quick reply keeps things moving.

parameters.content: Obligated is the right word, Hal. I wrote Thursday morning, eight o'clock, my porch, and I don't erase ink. Now sit and eat before Donna finishes the pot roast.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
